items.content:
You are prompting Claude Fable 5 like it is Claude 4.

12 prompts from Anthropic's official guide: 

1. Tell it when to act

Fable can burn minutes over-planning a simple job.

"When you have enough information to act, act. Give a recommendation, not a survey."

You get a decision, not a stalled plan.

2. Check its own progress

On long runs it used to report work it never did.

"Audit each claim against a tool result. If it isn't verified, say so."

No more fake "done".

3. Set boundaries

Fable takes action you never asked for, like an email.

"When I'm thinking out loud, the deliverable is your assessment. Report and stop."

It reports, then waits for you.

4. Only pause when needed

Left alone, it checks in far more than the work needs.

"Pause only when the work truly needs you: a destructive action or your input."

Fewer interruptions, more finished work.

5. Keep it running on long jobs

Deep in a session it stops and just states the plan.

"Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph. If it's a promise, do it now."

It finishes instead of describing.

6. Give it a memory

Without notes, it repeats mistakes it already made.

"Store one lesson per file. Record why it mattered. Update, don't duplicate."

It compounds what it learns.

7. Give it the reason

With no purpose, it guesses at what you actually want.

"I'm working on [TASK] for [WHO]. They need [OUTCOME]. With that: [REQUEST]."

Ten words of context, far sharper output.

8. Spin up parallel subagents

It spins up parallel workers more readily than old models.

"Delegate independent subtasks to subagents and keep working while they run."

Three jobs at once instead of one.

9. Lead with the outcome

Left alone, it buries the point under build-up.

"Lead with the outcome. Your first line is what happened, the detail comes after."

You get the answer first.

10. Write for the absent reader

After a long run its shorthand gets dense.

"Your summary is for someone who wasn't watching. Open with the outcome, no arrow chains."

The summary makes sense to anyone.

11. Don't over-engineer

On high effort it tidies and refactors past the task.

"Don't add features, refactor, or add abstractions beyond what the task requires."

It builds what you asked for, nothing more.

12. Verify with a fresh subagent

Self-review misses what a fresh agent catches.

"Every so often, have a fresh subagent check your work against the spec."

A real check before you ship.

Bonus tip: paste all 12 into your CLAUDE.md file. Then Fable 5 follows them in every chat, automatically.

Full guide is free here: https://lnkd.in/eS37Qz7s

items.content:
POV: You spent £4,143 to be at Cannes Lions 😭

and closed zero deals (it was worth every penny):

Naming that number feels gross.
The money was never the point.

So what did £4,143 actually buy?

Flights, accommodation, and a pass I barely used.

Everything that (actually) mattered came free:

☑︎ Exposure that levels you up, not instant ROI.
☑︎ Conversations I could not get by posting.
☑︎ Brunch with dream brands like OpenAI.
☑︎ A surprise invite to speak with Adobe.
☑︎ A party with Stan I will not forget.

None of it fit on a spreadsheet.

So yes, I am going back next year.

My tips if you are going too:

1. Tell everyone you are going.
2. Go with friends (it's way more fun).
3. Book early, or play catch-up like I did.
4. Make content, have fun, skip the FOMO.
5. You do not need a pass, only the right people.

That is when the best invites find you.

Proximity is the real product of Cannes.
You cannot download a room like that.

The brands and people who made it special:

- Olivia Owens and Kelly Song (Teachable)
- AJ Eckstein 🧩 (Creator Match 🧩)
- John Hu (Stan) and jt barnett
- Leila Woodington (OpenAI)
- Charlotte Sparks (Adobe)
- Fiona Turko (Gamma)

Applications to sponsor me next year are open 😉
Reach me at hello@charliehills.ai for more details.
